Genome / contig coverage plot

Source: R/mp_genomics.R
mp_coverage.Rd

Draws sequencing-depth (coverage) tracks along a genome or contig from a tidy data frame, a samtools depth / bedGraph / BED file, or – optionally – a BAM/CRAM alignment. Multiple samples are overlaid by colour and multiple contigs are faceted. Gene annotations and highlight regions can be overlaid.

Usage

mp_coverage(
  x,
  format = c("auto", "depth", "bedgraph", "bed", "bam", "data.frame"),
  region = NULL,
  window = NULL,
  contig = NULL,
  sample = NULL,
  plot.type = c("line", "area"),
  log.y = FALSE,
  annotations = NULL,
  highlight = NULL,
  palette = NULL,
  theme = NULL,
  ...,
  plot.title = NULL,
  plot.subtitle = NULL,
  plot.caption = NULL,
  font.size = getOption("micropubr.font.size", 11),
  return.data = FALSE,
  verbose = getOption("micropubr.verbose", FALSE)
)

Arguments

x

A data frame (with position/depth columns), a path to a samtools depth, bedGraph or BED file, or a path to a BAM/CRAM file.

format

Input format: "auto" (guess from extension/columns), "depth", "bedgraph", "bed", "bam" or "data.frame".

region

Optional region to restrict a BAM import, as "contig:start-end" or "contig".

window

Optional window size (bp) for binning to mean depth – useful for whole-genome views.

contig

Optional contig name(s) to keep.

sample

Optional sample label (for single-sample inputs).

plot.type

"line" or "area".

log.y

Plot depth on a log10 axis.

annotations

Optional gene track: a data frame with start, end and optionally strand and label columns (and contig for multi-contig views).

highlight

Optional data frame of regions to shade, with start and end (and optional contig).

palette, theme, plot.title, plot.subtitle, plot.caption, font.size

See mp_alpha().

...

Passed to the primary geom.

return.data

If TRUE, return the tidy coverage data frame.

verbose

Print the methods used.

Value

A ggplot object, or a data frame when return.data = TRUE.

Examples

cov <- data.frame(
  contig = "chr1", position = 1:500,
  depth = 50 + as.integer(20 * sin(seq(0, 6 * pi, length.out = 500)))
)
mp_coverage(cov, plot.type = "area")
